proposed_copy.title: Trump Commuted Mark Shapiro’s 85-Year Prison Sentence to Time Served
proposed_copy.description_short: A December 23, 2020 DOJ clemency warrant commuted Mark Shapiro’s 85-year prison term to time served, leaving restitution and supervised release in force.
proposed_copy.description_medium: On December 23, 2020, President Donald Trump commuted Mark Shapiro’s 1,020-month (85-year) prison sentence to time served. The DOJ warrant left the remaining restitution balance, a $500 special assessment, and a three-year term of supervised release in force. DOJ’s index lists securities, wire, and mail fraud convictions and $22,075,631 in restitution. The White House cited time served beyond the plea offer and support from advocates and victims as its rationale; that is the administration’s account.
proposed_copy.description_long: On December 23, 2020, President Donald Trump signed an executive grant of clemency commuting Mark Shapiro’s 1,020-month (85-year) prison sentence to time served. The Justice Department’s warrant cites federal securities provisions and federal conspiracy, mail-fraud, and wire-fraud provisions, and records the sentence imposed on October 21, 2010: imprisonment, three years of supervised release, $22,075,631 in restitution, and a $500 special assessment. DOJ’s commutations index labels the convictions as securities, wire, and mail fraud. The warrant says Shapiro had remained confined since the jury verdict in November 2009 and was projected to be released in 2078. It states that Trump found the ends of justice did not require continued confinement and that community safety would not be compromised. The warrant left any unpaid restitution, the special assessment, the supervised-release term, and all other sentence components in force, and directed the Bureau of Prisons to release him after receiving the warrant. The White House separately said Shapiro’s sentence was over ten times the plea offer and cited time served and support from advocates and victims. That explanation is the administration’s stated rationale, not an independent finding about the fairness of the original sentence.
